slides.title: Interior and Exterior Angles of a Triangle
slides.note: Post the learning target. Say one line and nothing else yet: “Today the angles belong to a triangle: inside they make 180°, and an outside angle is the two far ones added.”

slides.title: Warm-Up
slides.sub: On your own. Four minutes. No notes.
slides.note: Q4 is Notes I before it is said: three angles along a straight line make 180°. Today's triangle puts its three corners there. Two minutes silent, then reveal.

slides.title: Warm-Up
slides.note: Reveal. Ask for the band each question came from only if time allows.

slides.title: Vocabulary
slides.sub: The new words, before they are used.
slides.note: Read each word and its meaning once; the notes use them next. Students copy the words, not the definitions.

slides.title: Notes
slides.sub: Copy the rule and the example.
slides.note:
Tear the three corners off a paper triangle and set them side by side: they fill a straight line, 180°. So the third angle is 180 minus the other two: 180 − 65 − 40 = 75. Every triangle, any shape or size.
OFF: 'Inside a triangle, the three make 180.'

slides.title: Notes
slides.note:
Extend one side: the exterior angle and the interior angle beside it are a linear pair, 180°. The interior angle is 180 minus the two remote ones, so the exterior angle IS the two remote ones: 50 + 70 = 120 (the state guide's item). Two named mistakes: the exterior angle is not the interior angle beside it (60°), and it is not the angle around the outside (240°). Each corner has two exterior angles, vertical to each other, so equal.
OFF: 'Outside equals the two far ones added.'

slides.title: Notes
slides.note:
The angles are x, x and 2x + 20: the Triangle Sum gives the equation, 4x + 20 = 180, so x = 40. Put x back: 40°, 40° and 100° — they add to 180, the check. The question asks for the angles, not x.
OFF: 'Write the sum, solve, put x back, check 180.'

slides.title: Example 1
slides.note: Ask what the three angles of any triangle add to before anyone subtracts: 180.

slides.title: Example 1
slides.note: 58 + 71 = 129, and 180 − 129 = 51°. A board with 231 added 180; one with 129 stopped at the sum.

slides.title: Your Turn
slides.sub: Same steps, your numbers. Boards up when done.
slides.note: 39 + 84 = 123, so 180 − 123 = 57°. A board with 123 stopped at the sum.

slides.title: Your Turn
slides.note: Reveal; name what a wrong board most likely did (see the note above).

slides.title: Example 2
slides.note: Ask which two angles are remote — not touching the exterior angle: the 64° and the 49°.

slides.title: Example 2
slides.note: The Exterior Angle Theorem: x = 64 + 49 = 113°. Check by the long way: the interior angle beside it is 180 − 113 = 67°, and 64 + 49 + 67 = 180. A board with 67 found the interior angle, not the exterior one.

slides.title: Your Turn
slides.sub: Same steps, your numbers. Boards up when done.
slides.note: 72 + 35 = 107°. A board with 73 found the interior angle beside it.

slides.title: Your Turn
slides.note: Reveal; name what a wrong board most likely did (see the note above).
